messages:
Priya - CS: FYI customer CS-9876 on Dedicated (pool ded-4321) in na-south reports spike of 429s and auth failures since earlier evict/reroute. They see partial success but many requests returning 401/429. Affects all model variants.
Mia - Support: Got the ticket. They pasted sample error: `{"error":"auth_failed","code":401}` and also intermittent `429` with body `rate_limit_exceeded`. They claim they didn't change client config.
Ajay - SRE: Noted. I see region autoscaler logged an evacuation of two hosts at 03:42 UTC due to preemptions, then placement retries. Might be a placement storm plus noisy-tenant backpressure. Checking placement logs now.
Elena - Eng Runtime: If autoscaler removed nodes while prefix cache was warm, requests may hit fallback path that triggers per-tenant throttle. Also older auth tokens might have been invalidated if control-plane pod restarted. Do we have control-plane restarts in na-south?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: control-plane/manager restarted on na-south-control-az2 at 03:41:57 UTC (reason: kernel OOM).
Ajay - SRE: That matches. OOM triggered evacuation; scale-down then scale-up created a burst of placement requests. Some placement attempts hit remote region fallback -> cross-region token validation path which has stricter rate limits.
Mia - Support: Customer says billing meter shows weird zero-usage windows then a big spike, and invoice preview differs from their expected commit. They want credits for the outage window. Ticket updated with logs and repro steps.
Raj - Billing: We'll freeze billing adjustments for CS-9876 pending triage. I need the exact outage window and request ids.
Priya - CS: Provided sample request ids and a short repro: 1) Send a long chat stream to Dedicated endpoint (dedicated-na-south.drw/api/v1/generate) 2) After a few tokens, client receives 401 then client retries and hits 429. Attached curl sample.
Mia - Support: Pasting minimal repro curl:
```
curl -X POST https://dedicated-na-south.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v1","input":"hello","stream":false}'
```
Response sequence: 200 -> 401 -> 429 on retries.
Elena - Eng Runtime: Can you grab the request_id header values from the failed responses? Need `x-rw-req` to trace through routing.
Priya - CS: Provided three ids: rw-req-00123, rw-req-00124, rw-req-00125.
Ajay - SRE: Traced rw-req-00124: placed on host host-az2-07, then evicted, then retried to host-az1-02 which is in a different capacity tier and uses the auth proxy v2 leading to token validation mismatch for some older tokens. Root cause hypothesis: control-plane restart + cross-tier reroute causing transient auth cache misses and a per-tenant emergency throttle kick-in.
Elena - Eng Runtime: Agree. There's a missing compatibility check in the reroute flow: if the destination host uses auth-proxy v2 and the token was minted before switch, validation path rejects it instead of falling back to legacy validation. I can prototype a patch to accept legacy tokens for 10 mins post-reroute.
Mia - Support: Customer also reported noisy neighbor CPU spikes on ded-4321 pool around the same time. Any evidence of noisy tenant?
Ajay - SRE: Yes, tenant t-987 (internal test workload) did 1000 short requests causing high scheduling jitter. Autoscaler reacted slowly due to blocked placement queue. That contributed to queueing and the retried placements.
Elena - Eng Runtime: Mitigations: 1) short-term: add cross-auth fallback to avoid 401 on retried placements; 2) medium-term: make reroute token compatibility check permissive for 5-15 minutes after control-plane deployment; 3) limit noisy tenant burst by enforcing per-tenant concurrency caps at placement layer.
Mia - Support: For customer communication: explain root cause, confirm we will credit the outage window, and share repro and resolution ETA.
Raj - Billing: Confirmed will hold credits; need official SLA hit request from CS.
Ajay - SRE: Operational actions I will take now: - isolate noisy tenant t-987 (rate-limit and pause workload) - temporarily increase ded-4321 reserve instances (+2) in na-south to absorb burst - set placement retry jitter to 250ms to smooth retries.
Ajay - SRE: Commands I'm running:
```
# pause test tenant
./ctl tenants pause t-987 --reason="noisy-tenant evict"
# bump reservation
./ctl pools resize ded-4321 --add 2 --region na-south
# adjust jitter
./ctl config set placement.retry_jitter_ms 250 --region na-south
```
Elena - Eng Runtime: I'll open a hotfix PR for token compatibility and run quick e2e in staging. If green, roll to na-south with a canary.
Mia - Support: I'll update the customer: explain OOM -> evacuation -> reroute -> auth fallback bug -> noisy tenant contributed. Apologize and offer credit; give ETA 2-3 hours for hotfix canary and 24h for permanent mitigations.
Priya - CS: Customer accepted interim credit and wants confirmation when the hotfix is live. I'll mark ticket high priority.
Ajay - SRE: Monitoring: watch for 401/429 error rate returning to baseline, placement latency, and reserve pool fill. I'll post back when stable.
ops-bot: monitoring: 5m rolling 401 rate for ded-4321: 0.02% -> 0.9% at peak -> now 0.08%. 429 rate: peaked 1.2% -> now 0.11%.
Ajay - SRE: Good, rates dropping. Leaving temporary reservation for 6 hours.
Elena - Eng Runtime: PR opened: r/engine/runtime#5892 (hotfix token-compat). Can deploy 1 canary in na-south when Ajay gives the go.
Ajay - SRE: Go for canary.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: runtime/token-compat deployed canary on na-south-az1 at 04:12 UTC.
Priya - CS: Notified customer that canary is rolling; they confirmed improvements. Closing loop after 24h follow-up. :thumbsup:
